stories.title: Four arrested over fatal shooting of South African boxer Zolani Tete
stories.summary: Tete, who won world WBF flyweight and WBO bantamweight titles, was killed outside his home in Eastern Cape last week. South African police say they have arrested four people in connection with the murder of two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete, who was shot last week. The four suspects arrested over the weekend are aged between 22 and 28, police said in a statement on Monday. One has been formally charged with murder. Tete, 38, was attacked on Friday evening as he returned to his home in Mdantsane in the Eastern Cape province. A 27-year-old woman who was with him in the car survived but is in hospital, police said. Tete won the IBF junior bantamweight world title in 2014 and the WBO bantamweight world title in 2017. In 2017, he entered boxing history when he took just 11 seconds to flatten his opponent with his first punch to retain his WBO bantamweight crown. It was the fastest knockout victory in a world championship bout. In 2023, the United Kingdom Anti-Doping agency hit Tete with a four-year ban that ended on July 29, and he was preparing to return to professional boxing. “South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced,” Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said in a statement following the murder. “He was training for a return to the ring.

stories.title: Chad accuses Sudanese army of targeting convoy in Chadian territory
stories.summary: Military authorities in Chad have accused Sudan of launching drone strikes against a convoy inside Chadian territory. The attack took place on Thursday and reportedly targeted the vehicles in East Ennedi province, more than 100 kilometres from the border with Sudan. The incident is raising fears that the war in Sudan could escalate regional tensions. Sudan has previously accused Chad of supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces who have been fighting the Sudanese army for control of Sudan since April 2023. Khartoum says N'djamena allows fighters and military supplies to transit through Chad. Chad has placed military units on high alert and warned warring parties in Sudan against crossing its frontier, saying it reserves the right to defend its territory.

stories.title: Chinese envoy hails Moscow Zoo for creating great atmosphere for pandas
stories.summary: Zhang Hanhui also congratulated panda Katyusha on her birthday
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.
Pandas at the Moscow Zoo couldn't ask for better care, Chinese Ambassador to Russia Zhang Hanhui told reporters at a ceremony marking panda Katyusha’s third birthday.
The diplomat praised the zoo staff for doing an excellent job.
"Chinese pandas live in Russia," the ambassador stressed, emphasizing the word "live." "I believe they feel better here.
They're doing as good as can be."
Zhang Hanhui also congratulated Katyusha on her birthday, calling her birth and growth a positive result of Chinese-Russian friendship.

stories.title: America’s US$40tr debt gamble is getting harder to ignore, economists say after ‘grow’ goal
stories.summary: With Washington claiming that the United States can “grow” out of its mounting fiscal burdens, some economists are sceptical that growth alone could absorb the country’s mountain of national debt, which just surpassed US$40 trillion. The milestone, reached last week, has amplified concerns about the long-term sustainability of maintaining such a massive debt pile – one that has doubled in size from a decade ago. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the trajectory last week, telling CNBC...
